sector: Retail (Amazon e-commerce retail supply chain: vendors, purchase orders, fulfilment warehouses, customer outbound)
hitl_conditions: Not explicitly discussed; implicitly, ML emulators are accepted only when explainable (monotonic input-output relations matching business intuition) to earn stakeholder trust; users choose models by accuracy/explainability/speed and define interventions, keeping decisions outside the simulator.
key_finding: SEmulate replaces the computationally expensive OR order-placing optimisation inside Amazon's digital-twin supply chain simulator with monotonic XGBoost emulators plus ML vendor fill-rate predictors, keeping physics-based inbound/outbound logic; runtime falls ~90% (orders of magnitude) with ~3% accuracy loss, enabling rapid, interpretable counterfactual experimentation for decision-makers.

Twin/validation evidence: Abstract and Section 1 (pp. 462-463, 'digital-twin based simulator' integrating production systems); 4.5 (p. 472, simulated inbound volume compared against real-world volume). HITL evidence: Section 1 (p. 463, explainability needed to earn stakeholder trust); Section 2 end (p. 466, desktop platform for users to test interventions); Section 3.1 (p. 466, explainability must align with business intuition; users specify model choice); 4.1 (p. 469, business adjusts labour planning and capacity control from estimated impacts).

quotes.text: Traditional digital-twin simulators, which are powered by complex optimization algorithms, are high-fidelity but can be computationally expensive and difficult to experiment with.
we compare the simulated inbound inventory volume against the real world volume for both the baseline simulator and SEmulate, where we do not observe tangible degradation on accuracy.

The novelty of SEmulate lies in that instead of solving the complex optimization, we utilize existing data and leverage ML to learn the relationship between the input features and the optimized decisions.
For our use case, we balance the three evaluation metrics in Table 1 and choose the monotonic XgBoost model with monotone constraints
one of the biggest drawback of emulators is that it lacks explainability especially for black-box models, and is hard to earn trust with stakeholders on the reliability of the models.
This light-weight hybrid simulator can easily run on desktops, offering a rapid and quick experimentation platform for users to test out different interventions.
